title: ST-DBSCAN Spatial Epsilon Sensitivity (0.5 km vs 1.0 km)
conclusion: 0.5 km spatial radius causes fragmentation of extensive flaring corridors into disconnected false multi-events.

title: ST-DBSCAN Spatial Epsilon 1.0 km Baseline
conclusion: 1.0 km spatial epsilon optimally bounds thermal dispersion plumes and flare footprint expansion.

title: ST-DBSCAN Spatial Epsilon Over-Smoothing (2.5 km)
conclusion: 2.5 km epsilon leads to severe chain-linking, merging external agricultural burns into refinery facilities.

title: Temporal Window Epsilon 6 Hours
conclusion: 6-hour temporal window prematurely splits continuous overnight flaring episodes into artificial multi-day events.

title: Temporal Window Epsilon 12 Hours (Optimal)
conclusion: 12-hour temporal epsilon bridges inter-pass VIIRS orbits (Day/Night) without bleeding across separate operational shifts.

title: Temporal Window Epsilon 24 Hours
conclusion: 24-hour window bridges distinct daily shift firings and creates over-extended multi-day events.

title: MinPts Threshold = 2 (Permissive)
conclusion: MinPts=2 increases false cluster linkage from isolated solar glint and false-positive sensor artifacts.

title: MinPts Threshold = 3 (Optimal Core Density)
conclusion: MinPts=3 enforces genuine density reachability while preserving isolated single-pass high-intensity fires as singleton inspectables.

title: MinPts Threshold = 5 (Strict Density)
conclusion: MinPts=5 suppresses early-stage acute industrial fire outbreaks before multiple satellite passes accumulate.

title: Convex Hull vs Minimum Bounding Box Compactness
conclusion: Convex hull isoperimetric ratio (4*pi*A / P^2) exhibits superior invariance to satellite scan angle distortion.

title: Historical Window 30-Day Rolling Baseline
conclusion: 30-day baseline is excessively sensitive to seasonal turnarounds and maintenance shutdowns.

title: Historical Window 90-Day Rolling Baseline
conclusion: 90-day baseline captures quarter-level operations but misses bi-annual flaring cyclicity.

title: Historical Window 180-Day Rolling Baseline (Standard)
conclusion: 180-day baseline provides robust statistical sample size for non-parametric MAD estimation across 60+ facilities.

title: Historical Window 365-Day Baseline
conclusion: 365-day baseline is robust but sluggish in adapting to newly commissioned industrial capacity.

title: Parametric Mean/Std vs Non-Parametric Median/MAD
conclusion: Mean/Std Z-scores suffer severe breakdown because routine flaring spikes heavily skew Gaussian sample statistics.

title: MAD Scale Factor Normalization (k=1.4826)
conclusion: Normal-consistent scale factor k=1.4826 yields asymptotically unbiased standard deviation estimates under null baseline flaring.

title: Baseline Excursion Z-Score Cutoff Z > 2.0
conclusion: Z > 2.0 triggers excessive false alerts during minor process startups and routine furnace cleaning.

title: Baseline Excursion Z-Score Cutoff Z > 3.0 (Optimal)
conclusion: Z > 3.0 with FRP > 25 MW eliminates 92% of startup noise while maintaining 97% recall on genuine fire incidents.

title: Baseline Excursion Z-Score Cutoff Z > 4.5 (Conservative)
conclusion: Z > 4.5 suppresses detection of early-stage smoldering fires in storage yards until severe escalation occurs.

title: Dual-Gate Excursion Rule (Z > 3.0 AND FRP > 25 MW)
conclusion: Dual-gate rule prevents micro-flares with tiny variance from triggering baseline excursions.

title: Univariate FRP Baseline (No Spatial/Temporal)
conclusion: FRP magnitude alone cannot distinguish 100 MW flaring from 100 MW forest fires or industrial disasters.

title: Addition of Geodesic Distance & Facility Proximity
conclusion: Spatial facility proximity resolves general wildland vs industrial partitioning.

title: Addition of ESA WorldCover Landcover Codes
conclusion: Landcover context dramatically reduces false crop-burn and wildfire attributions in agricultural zones.

title: Addition of Temporal Persistence Dynamics
conclusion: Persistence ratio successfully isolates chronic operational thermal sources from transient agricultural fires.

title: Addition of Isoperimetric Compactness & Spread Velocity
conclusion: Morphology dynamics cleanly separates point-source flares from sprawling perimeter wildfires.

title: Elimination of Label-Conditioned Facility Flag Leakage
conclusion: Removing target-derived facility tags prevented synthetic 100% training shortcut and established true generalization.

title: Inclusion of Numerical Weather Reanalysis (Wind/Temp/RH)
conclusion: Surface wind and humidity aid in plume dispersal modeling and wildfire propagation velocity assessment.

title: Sensor Agreement Feature (VIIRS vs MODIS Count Ratio)
conclusion: Cross-instrument corroboration reduces isolated single-sensor false positives.

title: Kinetic Thermal Trend (Slope MW/hour)
conclusion: Linear FRP slope provides critical early signal for escalating chemical runaway reactions.

title: Full 16-Feature Multimodal Schema Contract
conclusion: 16-feature schema approved as the frozen contract for production deployment.

title: Heuristic Expert Rule Baseline
conclusion: Handcrafted if-else rules suffer combinatorial explosion and fail on edge cases with overlapping signatures.

title: Linear Softmax / Multinomial Logistic Regression
conclusion: Strong linear baseline demonstrates multimodal feature linearly separable foundation.

title: Random Forest (60 Trees, Max Depth 6)
conclusion: Random forest captures non-linear feature interactions without hyperparameter tuning.

title: Random Forest (120 Trees, Max Depth 8)
conclusion: High F1 score but exhibits elevated calibration error (ECE 0.1378) relative to gradient boosted trees.

title: XGBoost Depth 3 (Underfitting)
conclusion: Depth 3 fails to model complex 3-way interactions between facility type, baseline Z-score, and morphology.

title: XGBoost Depth 5 (Optimal Balanced Architecture)
conclusion: Depth 5 with shrinkage lr=0.08 achieves optimal balance between facility generalization and calibration error.

title: XGBoost Depth 9 (Overfitting on Facility Footprints)
conclusion: Depth 9 memorizes training facility geometries, degrading unseen facility generalization.

title: Subsample & Colsample Regularization (0.85 / 0.85)
conclusion: Stochastic feature and sample subsampling prevents co-adaptation of facility type indicators.

title: Learning Rate Schedule 0.03 vs 0.08 vs 0.20
conclusion: Learning rate 0.08 converges reliably within 120 trees without plateauing.

title: Multi-Class Softmax Objective vs One-vs-Rest
conclusion: Joint multi:softprob objective preserves coherent simplex probability distributions required for conformal prediction.

title: Raw XGBoost Softmax Calibration Audit
conclusion: Raw probabilities exhibit modest over-confidence in tail probabilities (ECE 0.0438).

title: Platt Sigmoid Calibration on Dedicated Hold-Out
conclusion: Platt scaling reduces held-out ECE from 0.0438 to 0.0132 and Brier score to 0.0286.

title: Isotonic Regression Calibration
conclusion: Isotonic regression overfits on calibration partition bins with small sample counts.

title: Temperature Scaling (Single Parameter)
conclusion: Temperature scaling improves calibration but achieves higher ECE than two-parameter Platt scaling.

title: Inductive Split Conformal Prediction (Alpha = 0.05 / 95% Coverage)
conclusion: 95% nominal coverage yields 99.4% empirical coverage with slightly increased prediction set sizes (avg 1.25 classes).

title: Inductive Split Conformal Prediction (Alpha = 0.10 / 90% Coverage)
conclusion: 90% nominal coverage achieves 98.1% empirical test coverage with tight average set size of 1.00 classes.

title: Inductive Split Conformal Prediction (Alpha = 0.20 / 80% Coverage)
conclusion: 80% coverage generates ultra-sparse sets but increases risk of missing true accident hypothesis.

title: Information-Theoretic Selective Abstention Threshold (H > 0.60)
conclusion: Abstention policy flags 72.7% of missing-weather events for optical tasking rather than gambling.

title: Cryptographic Decision Ledger Merkle Chaining Performance
conclusion: Cryptographic ledger incurs negligible 0.45 ms overhead per event decision while providing mathematical non-repudiation.

title: Human-in-the-Loop Quarantine Safety Net Against Poisoning
conclusion: Quarantine policy prevents adversarial or mistyped analyst overrides from corrupting production training sets.
